beats.subline: Thursday, October 29, 2026 close — a tech-led slide as Alphabet's post-earnings plunge reignited AI-spending worries ahead of Amazon and Intel results.
beats.body: Alphabet shares fell about 12.6%, erasing roughly $500 billion in value, after posting negative free cash flow for a second straight quarter on heavy AI spending; Amazon and Intel both slid in after-hours trading on their own earnings, while third-quarter GDP growth accelerated to a 3.4% annual rate and Eli Lilly hit an all-time high on strong results.

beats.headline: Near-final Israeli vote count flips the race, putting Netanyahu's bloc ahead as allies float a unity government with Eisenkot
beats.body: With 99.9% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc held 53 seats to Eisenkot's 48 — reversing Tuesday's exit polls — while Arab parties surged to a record 19 seats; Likud allies are now promoting a unity government that would include Eisenkot alongside Smotrich and Ben-Gvir but exclude the ultra-Orthodox parties until a conscription law passes, though Eisenkot has given no sign he would engage.

beats.headline: CENTCOM says it has cleared Hormuz's main shipping lanes of Iranian mines as Iran reports halting two more tankers
beats.body: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said after a helicopter flight over the Strait of Hormuz that the primary transit routes are now clear of mines laid by Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy and that more than 95% of vessels have transited safely despite what the command calls a severely weakened Iranian navy; separately, Iran's Guard navy said Thursday it halted two more tankers south of the strait for allegedly using an unauthorized route.

beats.headline: Anthropic reaffirms its $80 billion founder philanthropy pledge and sets up super-voting shares ahead of its IPO
beats.body: The company's IPO filing confirms Dario Amodei and the six other co-founders will dedicate 80% of their personal equity to charitable causes, while shareholders are also being asked to approve new shares giving the co-founders a combined 50.1% voting control and a separate commitment of 5% of company stock to a new public-benefit fund.
